A South Korean novelist, born in 1970 in Gwangju, who in 2024 became the first Korean writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature. Her father, Han Seung-won, is also a novelist.

  • The Vegetarian (2007) follows a woman who stops eating meat and slowly withdraws from her family. In Deborah Smith's English translation it won the Man Booker International Prize in 2016.
  • Human Acts (2014) is about the Gwangju Uprising of 1980, when the army killed protesters in her home city.
  • We Do Not Part (2021) deals with the Jeju massacre of 1948.

The Nobel committee praised prose that faces historical trauma and shows how fragile human life is. Her books are part of the wider rise of Korean culture abroad, alongside films, music and TV such as Squid Game, that marked South Korea in the 2010s and 2020s.
